goal: agentfiles doctor says when Claude Code did not load a plugin or skill the last sync installed, so a skill that syncs cleanly but never reaches the model is caught (ROADMAP R16, Claude Code half).
changed: agentfiles/loaded.py: reads Claude Code's init event from claude -p in an empty folder and kills it once the event arrives; compares its plugins and skills with the plugins and skill folders of the last sync's agentfiles-local marketplace.
agentfiles/cli.py: doctor runs that check, skipped with a -- line when claude is missing or the last sync installed no Claude Code plugins.
tests/test_loaded.py: compare() on each problem kind, and doctor after a real sync through a fake claude that replays an init event.
README.md: the doctor lines say what it now checks.
ROADMAP R16: status for the Claude Code half, with what was measured and why the first Done-when clause cannot be met as worded.

claims.claim: After a clean sync, doctor reports every agentfiles plugin and skill loaded; after a sync of a skill with no description it names that skill and exits 1; after the fix it exits 0.
claims.check: Under a scratch HOME with a local upstream source: bin/agentfiles sync base, then bin/agentfiles doctor with the real claude 2.1.325 (ok, exit 0); upstream alpha's description removed, sync exit 0, doctor prints 'skill agentfiles:alpha loaded only as a slash command' and exits 1; description restored, sync, doctor exit 0.
claims.remaining: Only Claude Code. Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and pi wait on R0 and H4.

claims.claim: On Beau's machine the check is clean: 8 of 8 agentfiles plugins and 28 of 28 skills loaded, with nothing extra.
claims.check: bin/agentfiles doctor from this branch on the real HOME prints 'Claude Code 2.1.325 loaded all 8 agentfiles plugins and 28 skills from the last sync'. Its exit 1 comes from the existing rex duplicate warning, not this check.

claims.claim: No skill header that agent-kit's tools/validate.py accepts makes Claude Code 2.1.325 drop the skill, except user-invocable: false, which hides it on purpose.
claims.check: About 35 header variants loaded with claude -p --plugin-dir: drops happen only without a usable string description (none, a mapping, a YAML error, a tab, no frontmatter) and with user-invocable: false. tools/validate.py check_skill run on those six: errors on the first five, a warning only on user-invocable.
claims.remaining: So the first Done-when clause cannot be met as written; rewording it is Beau's call.

claims.claim: Reading the init event sends nothing to the model.
claims.check: The process is killed when the init event arrives, which Claude Code emits before its first request; no usage was measured.
claims.remaining: It does run the user's SessionStart hooks, as any claude start does.

claims.claim: The suite passes and the lock is unchanged.
claims.check: make test (119 tests, OK), bin/agentfiles lock --frozen exit 0

next.item: Reword R16's first Done-when clause to the failure Claude Code actually has: a skill with no usable description, which sync installs.
next.why_now: As written it names a header that doesn't exist on Claude Code 2.1.325, so the item can't be closed.
next.impact: R16's Claude Code half can be marked done.

next.item: The other tools' half of doctor.
next.why_now: Not now: it needs how Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and pi report loaded skills, which H4 confirms on real machines.
next.impact: One command replaces the hand checks of R0 and R11.

release.note: agentfiles doctor now checks that Claude Code loaded every plugin and skill the last sync installed, and names a skill Claude Code keeps from the model because its header has no usable description.
